steps: Stay calm and speak clearly.
Say exactly where you are: the area, road, building and a landmark the driver can find.
Say what happened, how old the person is, and whether they are awake and breathing.
Give your phone number and keep the phone on, they may call back.
Do not hang up until they tell you to. They can guide you through first aid on the phone.
Send someone to the gate or road to show the ambulance the way, and unlock the door.
en.intro: In Kenya you can call 999 or 112 for an ambulance, free from any phone, even without airtime. The Kenya Red Cross emergency line is 1199.
en.after: Keep the person's medicine list and ID ready for the paramedics, and tell the family.

steps: Tulia na uongee waziwazi.
Eleza mahali hasa ulipo: eneo, barabara, jengo na alama ambayo dereva anaweza kuipata.
Eleza kilichotokea, umri wa mtu, na kama yuko macho na anapumua.
Toa nambari yako ya simu na uiache ikiwa wazi, wanaweza kukupigia tena.
Usikate simu mpaka wakuambie. Wanaweza kukuelekeza jinsi ya kutoa huduma ya kwanza kwenye simu.
Mtume mtu asimame langoni au barabarani kuonyesha gari la wagonjwa njia, na ufungue mlango.
sw.intro: Nchini Kenya unaweza kupiga 999 au 112 kuita gari la wagonjwa, bure kutoka simu yoyote, hata bila salio. Nambari ya dharura ya Kenya Red Cross ni 1199.
sw.after: Weka tayari orodha ya dawa za mgonjwa na kitambulisho chake kwa wahudumu wa afya, na uijulishe familia.

steps: Check for danger first, then shout their name and tap their shoulders.
If they do not respond, tilt their head back gently and lift the chin to open the airway.
Look, listen and feel for normal breathing for up to 10 seconds.

If they are breathing normally, roll them onto their side into the recovery position: the top leg bent at the knee to stop them rolling, the top hand under the cheek, head tilted back so the mouth points down.
Keep checking that they are still breathing normally until help arrives.
If they stop breathing normally or only gasp, start CPR straight away.
avoid: Do not give them anything to eat or drink.
Do not leave them alone.
Do not put a pillow under their head while they lie on their back, it can block the airway.
en.intro: Someone who does not respond but is breathing needs their airway kept open.
en.urgent: Call 999 or 112 now, or ask someone else to call while you help.
en.after: Keep them warm with a blanket and tell the paramedics how long they were unresponsive.

steps: Kwanza hakikisha hakuna hatari, kisha mwite kwa jina kwa sauti na umguse mabegani.
Asipojibu, rudisha kichwa chake nyuma polepole na uinue kidevu ili kufungua njia ya hewa.
Tazama, sikiliza na uhisi kama anapumua kawaida kwa hadi sekunde 10.
Kama anapumua kawaida, mlaze kwa ubavu katika mkao wa kupona (recovery position): mguu wa juu ukunje gotini asibingirike, mkono wa juu chini ya shavu, kichwa nyuma kidogo ili mdomo uelekee chini.
Endelea kuhakikisha bado anapumua kawaida mpaka msaada ufike.
Akiacha kupumua kawaida au anatweta tu, anza CPR mara moja.
avoid: Usimpe chakula wala kinywaji.
Usimwache peke yake.
Usiweke mto chini ya kichwa chake akiwa amelala chali, unaweza kuziba njia ya hewa.
sw.intro: Mtu asiyejibu lakini anapumua anahitaji njia yake ya hewa iwe wazi.
sw.urgent: Piga 999 au 112 sasa hivi, au mwombe mtu mwingine apige wakati wewe unasaidia.
sw.after: Mfunike kwa blanketi apate joto na uwaambie wahudumu wa afya muda gani hakujitambua.

steps: Kneel beside them on a firm surface, on the floor rather than a bed.
Put the heel of one hand in the centre of the chest, on the lower half of the breastbone, and your other hand on top.
Keep your arms straight and push straight down hard and fast, 5 to 6 cm deep, about 2 pushes every second (100 to 120 a minute).
Let the chest come all the way back up after each push.
If you are trained and willing, give 2 rescue breaths after every 30 pushes. If not, just keep pushing without stopping.
When the AED arrives, switch it on and follow its spoken instructions. Nobody touches the person while it checks or shocks.
Keep going until help takes over, the person starts breathing normally, or you are too exhausted to continue. If someone else can help, swap every 1 to 2 minutes.
avoid: Do not stop pushing to check for a pulse.
Do not be afraid of hurting them. Ribs can crack in older people, keep going anyway: without CPR they will not survive.
These steps are for adults. For a child or baby, give 5 rescue breaths first, then push about one third of the depth of the chest (two fingers for a baby), 30 pushes to 2 breaths.
en.intro: If someone is unresponsive and not breathing normally, their heart has probably stopped. CPR keeps blood flowing to the brain until help arrives.
en.urgent: Call 999 or 112 now and put the phone on speaker. If there is a defibrillator (AED) nearby and someone else can fetch it, send them. If you are alone, do not leave the person to look for one: AEDs are rare in Kenya, just keep doing CPR.
en.after: If they start breathing normally, put them in the recovery position and keep watching their breathing.

steps: Piga magoti kando yake akiwa juu ya sehemu ngumu, sakafuni badala ya kitandani.
Weka kisigino cha kiganja kimoja katikati ya kifua, nusu ya chini ya mfupa wa kifua, na kiganja kingine juu yake.
Nyoosha mikono na ubonyeze moja kwa moja chini kwa nguvu na haraka, kina cha sentimita 5 hadi 6, kama mara 2 kila sekunde (100 hadi 120 kwa dakika).
Acha kifua kirudi juu kabisa baada ya kila kubonyeza.
Kama umefunzwa na uko tayari, mpe pumzi 2 baada ya kila mabonyezo 30. Kama sivyo, endelea tu kubonyeza bila kusimama.
AED ikifika, iwashe na ufuate maelekezo yake ya sauti. Mtu yeyote asimguse mgonjwa wakati inapima au inashtua.
Endelea mpaka wahudumu wachukue nafasi, mtu aanze kupumua kawaida, au umechoka kabisa. Kama kuna mtu mwingine, badilishaneni kila dakika 1 hadi 2.
avoid: Usisimame kubonyeza ili kupima mapigo ya moyo.
Usiogope kumuumiza. Mbavu zinaweza kuvunjika kwa wazee, endelea tu: bila CPR hataishi.
Hatua hizi ni za watu wazima. Kwa mtoto au mtoto mchanga, mpe pumzi 5 kwanza, kisha bonyeza karibu theluthi moja ya kina cha kifua (vidole viwili kwa mtoto mchanga), mabonyezo 30 kwa pumzi 2.
sw.intro: Mtu asiyejibu na asiyepumua kawaida, huenda moyo wake umesimama. CPR husaidia damu kuendelea kufika kwenye ubongo mpaka msaada ufike.
sw.urgent: Piga 999 au 112 sasa hivi na uweke simu kwenye spika. Kama kuna mashine ya kushtua moyo (AED) karibu na kuna mtu mwingine wa kuileta, mtume. Kama uko peke yako, usimwache mgonjwa kwenda kuitafuta: AED ni chache Kenya, endelea tu na CPR.
sw.after: Akianza kupumua kawaida, mlaze katika mkao wa kupona na uendelee kuangalia anavyopumua.

steps: Ask "Are you choking?" If they can cough, encourage them to keep coughing.
If they cannot cough, speak or breathe, stand to the side and slightly behind them and lean them forward.
Give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand. Check after each one whether the object has come out.
If it has not cleared, give up to 5 abdominal thrusts: stand behind them, put your fist just above the belly button, hold it with your other hand, and pull sharply inwards and upwards.
Keep repeating 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until the object comes out or help arrives.
If they become unresponsive, lower them carefully to the floor, call 999 or 112 if nobody has, and start CPR.
avoid: Do not put your fingers in their mouth to feel for the object, you can push it deeper. Only remove something you can clearly see.
Do not give water while they are choking.

Do not give abdominal thrusts to a baby under 1. For a baby, give up to 5 back blows with the baby face down along your forearm, then up to 5 chest thrusts with two fingers on the breastbone, and call 999 or 112.
en.intro: Choking happens when something blocks the airway. If the person cannot cough, speak or breathe, act straight away.
en.urgent: Ask someone to call 999 or 112 while you start. If you are alone and it has not cleared after 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts, call 999 or 112 yourself straight away on speaker, then keep going.
en.after: Anyone who has had abdominal thrusts must see a doctor the same day, as they can cause internal injury.

steps: Muulize "Umekabwa?" Kama anaweza kukohoa, mhimize aendelee kukohoa.
Kama hawezi kukohoa, kuongea wala kupumua, simama kando yake na nyuma kidogo, kisha umwinamishe mbele.
Mpige makofi hadi 5 kwa nguvu katikati ya mabega kwa kisigino cha kiganja. Angalia baada ya kila kofi kama kitu kimetoka.
Kisipotoka, fanya mibano ya tumbo hadi 5: simama nyuma yake, weka ngumi juu kidogo ya kitovu, ishike kwa mkono mwingine, na uvute kwa nguvu ndani na juu.
Endelea kurudia makofi 5 na mibano ya tumbo 5 mpaka kitu kitoke au msaada ufike.
Akiacha kujitambua, mlaze sakafuni kwa uangalifu, piga 999 au 112 kama hakuna aliyepiga, na uanze CPR.
avoid: Usiingize vidole mdomoni kutafuta kitu, unaweza kukisukuma ndani zaidi. Toa tu kitu unachokiona waziwazi.
Usimpe maji wakati amekabwa.

Usimpe mtoto mchanga (chini ya mwaka 1) mibano ya tumbo. Kwa mtoto mchanga, mpe makofi hadi 5 mgongoni akiwa amelala kifudifudi juu ya mkono wako, kisha mibano hadi 5 ya kifua kwa vidole viwili juu ya mfupa wa kifua, na upige 999 au 112.
sw.intro: Kukabwa hutokea kitu kinapoziba njia ya hewa. Kama mtu hawezi kukohoa, kuongea wala kupumua, chukua hatua mara moja.
sw.urgent: Mwombe mtu apige 999 au 112 wakati wewe unaanza. Kama uko peke yako na kitu hakijatoka baada ya makofi 5 na mibano ya tumbo 5, piga 999 au 112 wewe mwenyewe mara moja kwa spika, kisha uendelee.
sw.after: Mtu yeyote aliyefanyiwa mibano ya tumbo lazima amwone daktari siku hiyo hiyo, kwani inaweza kusababisha jeraha la ndani.

ask.en: Can the person cough or speak?
ask.sw: Je, mtu huyo anaweza kukohoa au kuongea?

steps: Encourage them to keep coughing hard.
Stay with them and keep watching.
If they stop coughing, cannot speak or breathe, or start turning blue, start back blows and abdominal thrusts straight away.
avoid: Do not slap their back while they are coughing well.
Do not give water or food until it has cleared.
en.intro: If they can cough, speak or breathe, their airway is only partly blocked and coughing is the best way to clear it.
en.after: If they still feel something stuck, have pain, or keep coughing afterwards, take them to a doctor.

steps: Mhimize aendelee kukohoa kwa nguvu.
Kaa naye na uendelee kumwangalia.
Akiacha kukohoa, hawezi kuongea wala kupumua, au anaanza kubadilika rangi kuwa bluu, anza makofi ya mgongo na mibano ya tumbo mara moja.
avoid: Usimpige mgongoni wakati anakohoa vizuri.
Usimpe maji wala chakula mpaka kitoke.
sw.intro: Kama anaweza kukohoa, kuongea au kupumua, njia ya hewa imeziba kidogo tu na kukohoa ndiyo njia bora ya kukitoa.
sw.after: Kama bado anahisi kitu kimekwama, ana maumivu, au anaendelea kukohoa baadaye, mpeleke kwa daktari.

steps: Help them sit down in a comfortable half-sitting position, for example on the floor leaning against a wall with knees bent.
Loosen tight clothing and keep them calm and still.
If they are an adult, not allergic to aspirin, have no bleeding problem, and a doctor has not told them to avoid it, give one 300 mg aspirin to chew slowly.
If they have their own heart spray or tablets (GTN) prescribed for chest pain, help them take it as the doctor directed.
Stay with them and watch their breathing and how alert they are.
If they become unresponsive and stop breathing normally, start CPR.
avoid: Do not let them walk around, climb stairs or drive themselves to hospital.
Do not give food or drinks.
Do not wait to see if the pain goes away.
en.intro: Chest pain, pressure or tightness that may spread to the arm, jaw, neck or back, often with breathlessness, sweating or feeling sick, can be a heart attack. Older people, women and people with diabetes may only feel tired, breathless or unwell.
en.urgent: Call 999 or 112 now. Treat it as a heart attack until a doctor says otherwise.
en.after: Write down when the pain started and what medicine they took, and give this to the paramedics.

steps: Msaidie akae katika mkao wa nusu kukaa, kwa mfano sakafuni ameegemea ukuta na magoti yamekunjwa.
Legeza nguo zinazobana na umtulize asisogee.
Kama ni mtu mzima, hana mzio wa aspirini, hana tatizo la kutokwa damu, na daktari hajamkataza, mpe aspirini moja ya miligramu 300 aitafune polepole.
Kama ana dawa yake ya kupuliza au vidonge vya moyo (GTN) alivyoandikiwa kwa maumivu ya kifua, msaidie atumie kama daktari alivyoelekeza.
Kaa naye na uangalie anavyopumua na kama yuko macho.
Akiacha kujitambua na kuacha kupumua kawaida, anza CPR.
avoid: Usimwache atembee, apande ngazi wala ajiendeshe hospitalini.
Usimpe chakula wala vinywaji.
Usisubiri kuona kama maumivu yataisha.
sw.intro: Maumivu, mgandamizo au kubana kifuani kunakoweza kuenea mkononi, tayani, shingoni au mgongoni, mara nyingi pamoja na kukosa pumzi, kutokwa jasho au kichefuchefu, kunaweza kuwa mshtuko wa moyo. Wazee, wanawake na watu wenye kisukari wanaweza kuhisi uchovu tu, kukosa pumzi au kujisikia vibaya.
sw.urgent: Piga 999 au 112 sasa hivi. Lichukulie kama mshtuko wa moyo mpaka daktari aseme vinginevyo.
sw.after: Andika saa ambayo maumivu yalianza na dawa alizotumia, uwape wahudumu wa afya.

steps: Face: ask them to smile. Does one side of the face droop?
Arms: ask them to lift both arms. Does one drift down or feel weak?
Speech: is their speech slurred, strange or are they unable to speak or understand?
Time: call 999 or 112 straight away and note the exact time the signs started, doctors need this.
Also watch for sudden loss of balance, sudden loss of vision, a sudden very bad headache or sudden confusion.
Keep them comfortable, sitting or lying with head and shoulders slightly raised, and reassure them.
If they become unresponsive but are breathing, put them in the recovery position.
avoid: Do not give anything by mouth: no food, drink or medicine, including aspirin. Swallowing may be affected and they could choke.
Do not let them sleep it off or wait to see if it improves.
en.intro: A stroke is when blood stops reaching part of the brain. Every minute counts. Use the FAST check.
en.urgent: Call 999 or 112 now if you see any of these signs, even if they go away.
en.after: If the signs disappeared within minutes, it may have been a mini-stroke (TIA). They still need to see a doctor urgently today.

Usimwache alale ili ipite wala usisubiri kuona kama itaboreka.
sw.intro: Kiharusi ni pale damu inapoacha kufika sehemu ya ubongo. Kila dakika ni muhimu. Tumia kipimo cha FAST.
sw.urgent: Piga 999 au 112 sasa hivi ukiona dalili yoyote kati ya hizi, hata kama zitaisha.
sw.after: Kama dalili ziliisha ndani ya dakika chache, huenda ilikuwa kiharusi kidogo (TIA). Bado anahitaji kumwona daktari haraka leo.

steps: Put on gloves or use a plastic bag over your hand if you can, but do not delay.
Press firmly and directly on the wound with a clean cloth, pad or your hand.
Keep pressing hard without letting go until help arrives. Do not lift it to look.
If blood soaks through, remove the pad and press again firmly with a fresh pad straight away.
Once bleeding slows, tie a bandage or cloth firmly over the pad, not so tight that fingers or toes go cold or blue.

If it is an arm or leg, the bleeding is life-threatening and pressure is not stopping it, a tourniquet can be used by someone trained: 5 to 7 cm above the wound, tightened until bleeding stops, with the time written down.
Help them lie down. If they look pale, cold or sweaty, raise their legs and keep them warm.
avoid: Do not remove something stuck in the wound. Press around it instead.
en.intro: Heavy bleeding must be stopped quickly. Firm, direct pressure is the most important thing you can do.
en.urgent: Call 999 or 112 now, or ask someone else to call.
en.after: Tell the paramedics if the person takes blood thinners, such as warfarin or aspirin, as they will bleed more.

steps: Vaa glavu au funika mkono na mfuko wa plastiki kama unaweza, lakini usichelewe.
Bonyeza kwa nguvu moja kwa moja juu ya jeraha kwa kitambaa safi, pedi au mkono wako.
Endelea kubonyeza kwa nguvu bila kuachia mpaka msaada ufike. Usiinue kuangalia.
Damu ikilowesha pedi, iondoe na ubonyeze tena kwa nguvu mara moja kwa pedi mpya.
Damu ikipungua, funga bendeji au kitambaa kwa nguvu juu ya pedi, lakini si kwa kubana sana hadi vidole viwe baridi au bluu.
Kama ni mkono au mguu, damu ni hatari kwa maisha na kubonyeza hakuisimamishi, mtu aliyefunzwa anaweza kufunga tourniquet: sentimita 5 hadi 7 juu ya jeraha, kaza mpaka damu isimame, na uandike saa.
Msaidie alale chini. Akionekana mweupe, baridi au anatokwa jasho, inua miguu yake na umpe joto.
avoid: Usitoe kitu kilichokwama ndani ya jeraha. Bonyeza kuzunguka kitu hicho.
sw.intro: Damu nyingi lazima isimamishwe haraka. Kubonyeza kwa nguvu moja kwa moja kwenye jeraha ndiyo jambo muhimu zaidi unaloweza kufanya.
sw.urgent: Piga 999 au 112 sasa hivi, au mwombe mtu mwingine apige.
sw.after: Waambie wahudumu wa afya kama mtu anatumia dawa za kupunguza kuganda kwa damu, kama warfarin au aspirini, kwani atatokwa na damu zaidi.

steps: If they have an adrenaline auto-injector (such as an EpiPen), help them use it straight away into the outer thigh. It can go through clothing.
Hold it in place for as long as the device instructions say, then note the time.
If breathing is difficult, let them sit up. If they feel faint, lie them down with legs raised.
If there is no improvement after 5 minutes, or the symptoms come back, and they have a second injector, give the second dose.
Stay with them. If they become unresponsive and stop breathing normally, start CPR.
avoid: Do not wait to see if it gets better.
Do not let them stand up or walk suddenly, even if they feel better.
en.intro: A severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) can follow a sting, food or medicine. Signs include swelling of the lips, tongue or throat, wheezing or difficulty breathing, a hoarse voice, feeling faint, and often a rash.
en.urgent: Call 999 or 112 now.
en.after: They must go to hospital even if the adrenaline works, because the reaction can come back.

steps: Kama ana sindano ya adrenaline (kama EpiPen), msaidie aitumie mara moja kwenye upande wa nje wa paja. Inaweza kupita kwenye nguo.
Ishikilie kwa muda ambao maelekezo ya kifaa yanasema, kisha andika saa.
Kama anapumua kwa shida, mwache akae. Akihisi kuzimia, mlaze na uinue miguu yake.
Kama hakuna nafuu baada ya dakika 5, au dalili zinarudi, na ana sindano ya pili, mpe dozi ya pili.
Kaa naye. Akiacha kujitambua na kuacha kupumua kawaida, anza CPR.
avoid: Usisubiri kuona kama itapona.
Usimwache asimame wala atembee ghafla, hata akijisikia vizuri.
sw.intro: Mzio mkali (anaphylaxis) unaweza kufuata kuumwa na mdudu, chakula au dawa. Dalili ni kuvimba midomo, ulimi au koo, kupumua kwa shida au kwa mluzi, sauti kukwaruza, kuhisi kuzimia, na mara nyingi vipele.
sw.urgent: Piga 999 au 112 sasa hivi.
sw.after: Lazima aende hospitali hata kama adrenaline imesaidia, kwa sababu mzio unaweza kurudi.

what do i do during a fit
the old man is fitting and foaming at the mouth

steps: Stay calm and note the time the seizure started.
Move hard or sharp objects away and put something soft under their head.
Loosen anything tight around the neck, and remove glasses.
When the jerking stops, roll them onto their side into the recovery position and check their breathing.
Stay with them, talk calmly and reassure them until they are fully awake. They may be confused or sleepy for a while.
avoid: Do not hold them down or try to stop the movements.
Do not put anything in their mouth, they will not swallow their tongue.
Do not give food or drink until they are fully alert.
en.intro: During a seizure a person may fall, go stiff and jerk. Most seizures stop on their own within a few minutes. Your job is to keep them safe.
en.urgent: Call 999 or 112 if it lasts more than 5 minutes, it is their first seizure or the cause is unknown, another one follows, they are injured, they have trouble breathing afterwards, it happened in water, or they are not awake 10 minutes after it stops.
en.after: Write down how long it lasted and what happened, and tell their doctor and the family.

steps: Tulia na uandike saa kifafa kilipoanza.
Ondoa vitu vigumu au vyenye ncha karibu naye na uweke kitu laini chini ya kichwa chake.
Legeza kitu chochote kinachobana shingoni, na umvue miwani.
Kutetemeka kukiisha, mlaze kwa ubavu katika mkao wa kupona na uangalie anavyopumua.
Kaa naye, ongea kwa utulivu na umtulize mpaka azinduke kabisa. Anaweza kuchanganyikiwa au kusinzia kwa muda.
avoid: Usimshike kwa nguvu wala kujaribu kusimamisha mitikisiko.
Usiweke chochote mdomoni mwake, hatameza ulimi wake.
Usimpe chakula wala kinywaji mpaka azinduke kabisa.
sw.intro: Wakati wa kifafa mtu anaweza kuanguka, kukakamaa na kurusha viungo. Vifafa vingi huisha vyenyewe ndani ya dakika chache. Kazi yako ni kumweka salama.
sw.urgent: Piga 999 au 112 kama kinachukua zaidi ya dakika 5, ni mara yake ya kwanza au chanzo hakijulikani, kingine kinafuata, ameumia, anapumua kwa shida baadaye, kilitokea majini, au hajazinduka dakika 10 baada ya kuisha.
sw.after: Andika muda kilichodumu na kilichotokea, uwaambie daktari wake na familia.

examples: he is pale cold and sweaty after the accident
she looks grey and clammy and her pulse is fast
how to treat someone in shock
he is going into shock after losing blood
amepauka na ana baridi na jasho
mapigo yake ni ya haraka na dhaifu na ana jasho baridi

steps: Treat the cause if you can, for example press on a bleeding wound.
Help them lie down. Raise their legs if this does not hurt them and there is no injury to the legs, hips, back or head.
Loosen tight clothing and cover them with a blanket to keep them warm.
Reassure them and keep checking their breathing and how alert they are.
If they become unresponsive but are breathing, put them in the recovery position. If they stop breathing normally, start CPR.
avoid: Do not give food or drink. You can wet their lips if they are thirsty.
Do not leave them alone.
en.intro: Shock means not enough blood is reaching the organs, for example after heavy bleeding, burns, severe vomiting or diarrhoea, a serious infection or an allergic reaction. Signs are pale, cold, clammy skin, a fast weak pulse, fast breathing, dizziness and confusion.
en.urgent: Call 999 or 112 now.
en.after: Tell the paramedics what caused it and any changes you noticed.

steps: Tibu chanzo kama unaweza, kwa mfano bonyeza jeraha linalovuja damu.
Msaidie alale chini. Inua miguu yake kama haimuumizi na hakuna jeraha miguuni, kiunoni, mgongoni au kichwani.
Legeza nguo zinazobana na umfunike kwa blanketi apate joto.
Mtulize na uendelee kuangalia anavyopumua na kama yuko macho.
Akiacha kujitambua lakini anapumua, mlaze katika mkao wa kupona. Akiacha kupumua kawaida, anza CPR.
avoid: Usimpe chakula wala kinywaji. Unaweza kulowesha midomo yake akiwa na kiu.
Usimwache peke yake.
sw.intro: Mshtuko (shock) maana yake damu haitoshi kufika kwenye viungo, kwa mfano baada ya kutokwa damu nyingi, kuungua, kutapika au kuhara sana, maambukizi makali au mzio. Dalili ni ngozi nyeupe, baridi na yenye jasho, mapigo ya haraka na dhaifu, kupumua haraka, kizunguzungu na kuchanganyikiwa.
sw.urgent: Piga 999 au 112 sasa hivi.
sw.after: Waambie wahudumu wa afya kilichosababisha na mabadiliko uliyoyaona.

examples: we pulled him out of the water and he is not breathing
she nearly drowned in the pool
what to do for a drowning person

steps: Do not go into the water yourself unless trained. Reach with a stick or throw something that floats.
Once they are out, check if they are breathing normally.
If they are not breathing normally, give 5 rescue breaths if you can, then start CPR with 30 pushes and 2 breaths.
If they are breathing, put them in the recovery position so water can drain from the mouth.
Remove wet clothes if you can and cover them to keep them warm.
avoid: Do not press on the belly to push water out, it wastes time and can cause vomiting.
en.intro: A person pulled from water may have stopped breathing. Your safety comes first.
en.urgent: Call 999 or 112 now.
en.after: Anyone who was under water must go to hospital, even if they seem fine, as breathing problems can start hours later.

steps: Usiingie majini mwenyewe kama hujafunzwa. Mfikie kwa fimbo au mrushie kitu kinachoelea.
Akishatoka, angalia kama anapumua kawaida.
Kama hapumui kawaida, mpe pumzi 5 kama unaweza, kisha anza CPR kwa mabonyezo 30 na pumzi 2.
Kama anapumua, mlaze katika mkao wa kupona ili maji yatoke mdomoni.
Mvue nguo zilizolowa kama unaweza na umfunike apate joto.
avoid: Usibonyeze tumbo kutoa maji, inapoteza muda na inaweza kusababisha kutapika.
sw.intro: Mtu aliyetolewa majini huenda ameacha kupumua. Usalama wako ni wa kwanza.
sw.urgent: Piga 999 au 112 sasa hivi.
sw.after: Mtu yeyote aliyekuwa chini ya maji lazima aende hospitali, hata kama anaonekana mzima, kwani matatizo ya kupumua yanaweza kuanza saa kadhaa baadaye.

examples: what to do after an electric shock from a socket

steps: Switch off the power at the main switch or pull out the plug. Do not touch the person until the power is off.
If you cannot switch it off, stand on something dry like a wooden board or folded newspaper and push them away from the source with a dry wooden broom or chair.
For high-voltage power lines, stay at least 18 metres away and wait for Kenya Power or emergency services.
Once safe, check if they are breathing normally. If not, start CPR.
Cool any burns under cool running water for 20 minutes and cover them loosely with cling film or a clean cloth.
avoid: Do not touch them with bare hands while they are still in contact with electricity.
Do not use anything metal or wet to move them.
en.intro: Electricity can stop the heart and cause deep burns. Make it safe before you touch them.
en.urgent: Call 999 or 112 now.
en.after: Everyone who has had an electric shock should see a doctor, because it can affect the heart rhythm.

steps: Zima umeme kwenye swichi kuu au chomoa plagi. Usimguse mtu mpaka umeme uzimwe.
Kama huwezi kuzima, simama juu ya kitu kikavu kama ubao au gazeti lililokunjwa na umsukume mbali na chanzo kwa ufagio au kiti kikavu cha mbao.
Kwa nyaya za umeme mkubwa, kaa angalau mita 18 mbali na usubiri Kenya Power au huduma za dharura.
Ikiwa salama, angalia kama anapumua kawaida. Kama hapumui, anza CPR.
Poza majeraha ya moto chini ya maji baridi yanayotiririka kwa dakika 20 na uyafunike kwa ulegevu kwa karatasi ya plastiki au kitambaa safi.
avoid: Usimguse kwa mikono mitupu akiwa bado anagusa umeme.
Usitumie kitu cha chuma au chenye unyevu kumsogeza.
sw.intro: Umeme unaweza kusimamisha moyo na kusababisha kuungua kwa ndani. Hakikisha ni salama kabla ya kumgusa.
sw.urgent: Piga 999 au 112 sasa hivi.
sw.after: Kila aliyeshtuliwa na umeme amwone daktari, kwa sababu unaweza kuathiri mapigo ya moyo.

examples: he slipped and fell and can't get up
i found her on the floor
the old man fell out of bed
what to do when an elderly person falls
how do i help someone up after a fall
should i lift him after a fall

steps: Stay calm, check the area is safe, and talk to them. Ask what happened and where it hurts.
Check they are awake and breathing normally. If not, follow the unresponsive or CPR steps.
Look for injuries: bleeding, a head bump, pain in the hip or groin, or a leg that looks shorter or turned outwards, which can mean a broken hip.
If they are hurt or cannot get up, keep them still, put a pillow under the head only if there is no neck pain, cover them with a blanket and wait for help.

If they are not hurt and want to get up: help them roll onto their side, then onto hands and knees, crawl to a sturdy chair, put their hands on the seat, bring one foot forward and push up to turn and sit.
Let them rest, then check for dizziness, new pain or confusion over the next hours.
avoid: Do not lift them by yourself, you can injure both of you.
Do not give food or drink if they might have a broken bone, in case they need surgery.
en.intro: After a fall, an older person can be badly hurt without it being obvious. Do not rush to lift them.
en.urgent: Call 999 or 112 if they hit their head, were knocked out even briefly, take blood thinners, cannot move a leg, have severe pain in the hip, back or neck, are confused, or cannot get up.
en.after: Tell the family and their doctor about every fall, even if they seem fine. Falls can be a sign of illness, low blood pressure or medicine side effects.

steps: Tulia, hakikisha mahali ni salama, na uongee naye. Muulize kilichotokea na wapi panauma.
Hakikisha yuko macho na anapumua kawaida. Kama sivyo, fuata hatua za asiyejitambua au CPR.
Angalia majeraha: damu, uvimbe kichwani, maumivu kiunoni au kinena, au mguu unaoonekana mfupi au umegeukia nje, ambayo inaweza kumaanisha nyonga imevunjika.
Kama ameumia au hawezi kuinuka, mwache atulie, weka mto chini ya kichwa tu kama hana maumivu ya shingo, mfunike kwa blanketi na usubiri msaada.

Kama hajaumia na anataka kuinuka: msaidie ageuke kwa ubavu, kisha apige magoti na mikono chini, atambae hadi kiti imara, aweke mikono kwenye kiti, alete mguu mmoja mbele na ajisukume juu kugeuka na kukaa.
Mwache apumzike, kisha angalia kizunguzungu, maumivu mapya au kuchanganyikiwa kwa saa zinazofuata.
avoid: Usimwinue peke yako, mnaweza kuumia wote wawili.
Usimpe chakula wala kinywaji kama huenda amevunjika mfupa, kwa kuwa anaweza kuhitaji upasuaji.
sw.intro: Baada ya kuanguka, mzee anaweza kuwa ameumia vibaya bila kuonekana wazi. Usikimbilie kumwinua.
sw.urgent: Piga 999 au 112 kama aligonga kichwa, alipoteza fahamu hata kwa muda mfupi, anatumia dawa za kupunguza kuganda kwa damu, hawezi kusogeza mguu, ana maumivu makali kiunoni, mgongoni au shingoni, amechanganyikiwa, au hawezi kuinuka.
sw.after: Iambie familia na daktari wake kuhusu kila anguko, hata kama anaonekana mzima. Kuanguka kunaweza kuwa ishara ya ugonjwa, shinikizo la chini la damu au madhara ya dawa.

ask.en: Did they hit their head, or are they in severe pain?
ask.sw: Je, aligonga kichwa, au ana maumivu makali?

label.sw: Maumivu ya nyonga au mguu, hawezi kusimama

label.en: Not hurt, wants to get up

examples: i think she broke her arm
his leg looks bent after the fall
the bone is sticking out of the skin
she can't put weight on her leg and it's swollen
his leg is turned outwards and shorter
mguu wake umepinda baada ya kuanguka

steps: Keep them still and support the injured part in the position you found it, using pillows, rolled blankets or clothing.
For an arm, if they can bend it, support it in a sling made from a scarf or cloth.
If the bone has broken the skin, cover the wound with a clean dressing and press around it, not on the bone.
Put an ice pack wrapped in a cloth on the area for up to 20 minutes to reduce swelling.
Watch for signs of shock: pale, cold, sweaty skin or confusion.
avoid: Do not try to straighten the limb or push a bone back in.
Do not give food or drink, they may need surgery.
Do not move them if you suspect a hip, back or neck injury, unless they are in danger.
en.intro: Signs of a broken bone are pain, swelling, bruising, a limb at a strange angle, or not being able to move or put weight on it.
en.urgent: Call 999 or 112 for a suspected broken hip, thigh, pelvis, neck or back, a bone poking through the skin, or a limb that is cold, pale or numb below the injury. For other breaks, take them to hospital.
en.after: Older people often break a hip or wrist in a fall. Even if they can still walk, persistent pain needs an X-ray.

steps: Mwache atulie na usaidie sehemu iliyoumia ilivyo, kwa mito, blanketi zilizoviringishwa au nguo.
Kwa mkono, kama anaweza kuukunja, ushikilie kwa kombeo lililotengenezwa kwa skafu au kitambaa.
Kama mfupa umetoboa ngozi, funika jeraha kwa kitambaa safi na ubonyeze kuzunguka, si juu ya mfupa.
Weka barafu iliyofungwa kwenye kitambaa kwa hadi dakika 20 kupunguza uvimbe.
Angalia dalili za mshtuko: ngozi nyeupe, baridi, yenye jasho au kuchanganyikiwa.
avoid: Usijaribu kunyoosha kiungo wala kurudisha mfupa ndani.
Usimpe chakula wala kinywaji, anaweza kuhitaji upasuaji.
Usimsogeze ukishuku nyonga, mgongo au shingo imeumia, isipokuwa yuko hatarini.
sw.intro: Dalili za kuvunjika mfupa ni maumivu, uvimbe, michubuko, kiungo kilichopinda isivyo kawaida, au kushindwa kukisogeza au kukiwekea uzito.
sw.urgent: Piga 999 au 112 ukishuku nyonga, paja, fupanyonga, shingo au mgongo umevunjika, mfupa umetoboa ngozi, au kiungo ni baridi, cheupe au hakihisi chini ya jeraha. Kwa mivunjiko mingine, mpeleke hospitali.
sw.after: Wazee mara nyingi huvunjika nyonga au kifundo cha mkono wanapoanguka. Hata kama bado anatembea, maumivu yanayoendelea yanahitaji X-ray.

examples: his ankle is swollen after slipping
pulled a muscle in his back
big bruise on her leg after bumping the table
his knee is swollen and painful after twisting it

steps: Rest: stop using the injured part and help them sit or lie down.
Ice: put an ice pack or cold wet cloth wrapped in a towel on it for 15 to 20 minutes, every 2 to 3 hours for the first 2 days.
Compression: wrap it with an elastic bandage, firm but not tight. Loosen it if toes or fingers go cold, blue or numb.
Elevation: raise the injured part on pillows, above the level of the heart if possible.
Paracetamol can help with pain if it is safe with their other medicines.
avoid: Do not put ice directly on the skin.
Do not use heat, massage or rub the area for the first 2 days.
en.intro: Twisting a joint or pulling a muscle causes pain, swelling and bruising. Most improve with simple care.
en.after: See a doctor if they cannot put weight on it, the pain is severe, it looks deformed, there is numbness, or it is not better in a few days. In older people after a fall, it may be a fracture.

steps: Pumzika: acha kutumia sehemu iliyoumia na umsaidie akae au alale.
Barafu: weka barafu au kitambaa baridi chenye maji kilichofungwa kwenye taulo kwa dakika 15 hadi 20, kila saa 2 hadi 3 kwa siku 2 za kwanza.
Kubana: zungushia bendeji ya kunyooka, ikaze lakini isibane sana. Ilegeze vidole vikiwa baridi, bluu au havihisi.
Kuinua: inua sehemu iliyoumia juu ya mito, juu ya usawa wa moyo kama inawezekana.
Paracetamol inaweza kusaidia maumivu kama ni salama pamoja na dawa zake nyingine.
avoid: Usiweke barafu moja kwa moja kwenye ngozi.
Usitumie joto, kukanda wala kusugua sehemu hiyo kwa siku 2 za kwanza.
sw.intro: Kuteguka kiungo au kuvuta msuli husababisha maumivu, uvimbe na michubuko. Mingi hupona kwa huduma rahisi.
sw.after: Mwone daktari kama hawezi kukanyaga, maumivu ni makali, kiungo kimepinda, hakihisi, au hakijapona kwa siku chache. Kwa wazee baada ya kuanguka, huenda ni kuvunjika.

title.sw: Kuteguka, mshtuko wa msuli au mchubuko

examples: he hit his head when he fell
she banged her head on the door
bump on the head what to watch for
he hit his head and is vomiting
grandma fell and hit her head and takes warfarin
there is a lump on his head after the fall
should i let him sleep after a head injury

kichwa kimepasuka kidogo na kinavuja damu
dalili za hatari baada ya kugonga kichwa

steps: Help them sit down and rest.
Hold a cold pack wrapped in a cloth on the bump for 10 to 20 minutes.
If there is a cut, press on it with a clean cloth to stop the bleeding.
Make sure someone stays with them for the next 24 hours and checks on them regularly, including waking them gently if they sleep.
Watch for any of the danger signs above and call for help straight away if they appear.
avoid: Do not leave them alone for the first 24 hours.
Do not give alcohol or sleeping tablets.
If you suspect a neck injury, do not move them.
en.intro: Most bumps to the head are minor, but older people and anyone on blood thinners can bleed inside the skull, sometimes hours later.
en.urgent: Call 999 or 112 if they were knocked out even briefly, are confused or very drowsy, vomit more than once, have a severe or worsening headache, have a seizure, have blood or clear fluid from the ears or nose, have weakness, slurred speech, unequal pupils, double vision, loss of balance or memory, or difficulty walking. Anyone over 65, on blood thinners, who has had brain surgery or has been drinking alcohol should be checked at a hospital or clinic today.
en.after: Tell the family and the doctor about the head injury, even if it seemed small.

steps: Msaidie akae na apumzike.
Shikilia barafu iliyofungwa kwenye kitambaa juu ya uvimbe kwa dakika 10 hadi 20.
Kama kuna jeraha, libonyeze kwa kitambaa safi kusimamisha damu.
Hakikisha mtu anakaa naye kwa saa 24 zijazo na anamwangalia mara kwa mara, hata kumwamsha polepole akilala.
Angalia dalili zozote za hatari hapo juu na uite msaada mara moja zikitokea.
avoid: Usimwache peke yake kwa saa 24 za kwanza.
Usimpe pombe wala vidonge vya usingizi.
Ukishuku shingo imeumia, usimsogeze.
sw.intro: Michubuko mingi ya kichwa ni midogo, lakini wazee na yeyote anayetumia dawa za kupunguza kuganda kwa damu wanaweza kuvuja damu ndani ya fuvu, wakati mwingine saa kadhaa baadaye.
sw.urgent: Piga 999 au 112 kama alipoteza fahamu hata kwa muda mfupi, amechanganyikiwa au anasinzia sana, anatapika zaidi ya mara moja, ana maumivu makali ya kichwa au yanayozidi, anapata kifafa, anatokwa damu au maji meupe masikioni au puani, ana udhaifu, maneno hayatoki vizuri, mboni za macho hazilingani, anaona vitu viwili, anapoteza usawa au kumbukumbu, au anatembea kwa shida. Yeyote mwenye zaidi ya miaka 65, anayetumia dawa za kupunguza kuganda kwa damu, aliyefanyiwa upasuaji wa ubongo au aliyekunywa pombe akigonga kichwa achunguzwe hospitali au kliniki leo.
sw.after: Iambie familia na daktari kuhusu jeraha la kichwa, hata kama lilionekana dogo.

examples: he fell from a ladder and his neck hurts
she can't feel her legs after the fall
possible spinal injury what to do
should i move someone with a back injury
tingling in his arms after hitting his head
ameanguka kutoka kwenye ngazi na shingo inauma
hawezi kuhisi miguu baada ya kuanguka
